_about: Generated by tools/fixes/build.py from fixes/<id>/fix.json; do not edit (edit the fix's own file, then run python3 tools/fixes/build.py). Every device fix GameCove knows: what it changes, how it's undone, who gets it (auto / optional: selectors over devices.json traits, docs/DEVICES.md; devices: the same, resolved), whether it's Recommended or Optional, and its lifecycle rules (needed_when / obsolete_when: conditions the handheld checks itself; watch: what the nightly audit follows). docs/FIXES.md explains every field. The nightly "fixes" data release is this file plus what the audit observed.

fixes.title: MSI buttons
fixes.line: Makes the two MSI buttons next to the screen work: left opens the menu, right opens Quick Access.
fixes.symptom: Both MSI face buttons do nothing in Gaming Mode: the firmware sends Win+G and F15, InputPlumber's stock map waits for other keys.
fixes.why: InputPlumber's stock config for board MS-1T91 (firmware E1T91) waits for keys this firmware never sends; other Claw firmwares send what their configs expect.
fixes.risk_note: Only adds two InputPlumber files in /etc; the stock files are never edited.

changes.detail: A button map: Guide = G, Quick Access = F15, M1/M2 back buttons.
A copy of InputPlumber's own file for this board that points at the map above (rebuilt when the stock file changes).
Restarted once so it reads the new files.

fixes.undo: Deletes both files and restarts InputPlumber, which then reads its stock files again.
fixes.bazzite: Not fixed (InputPlumber still maps the board to claw2).
sources: ClawDeck docs/HARDWARE-FINDINGS.md section 12 (measured with evtest on BIOS E1T91IMS.10D)

probe.what: Reads InputPlumber's own capability map for this board and checks it takes what this firmware sends (Guide from G or Win+G, Quick Access from F15 alone), from the map itself, not its name. Until ours is removed, the no-password rebuild keeps InputPlumber's map in the override, and conflict=no says ours stands aside.

watch.note: The stock config our override shadows: a new capability_map_id means it's fixed upstream.
A release may carry the fix.
A BIOS that sends other keys for the MSI buttons changes what the map must wait for.

fixes.title: Smooth screen down to 30 fps
fixes.line: Lets VRR keep games smooth down to 30 fps instead of 48.
fixes.symptom: The Claw's panel EDID says 48-120 Hz although the panel does 30-120 Hz, so VRR stops working under 48 fps.
fixes.why: The panel: the CSW PN8007QB1-2 in the Claw 8 AI+ and 8 EX (and the TMX TL070FVXS02-0 in the A1M and 7 AI+) report 48-120 Hz but run 30-120 Hz; the fix only patches those exact factory EDIDs (sha256) and hooks the Intel GPU driver.
fixes.risk_note: Changes what the Intel GPU driver is told about the panel at boot. Only exact, validated factory EDIDs are patched, and a boot-menu kill switch (gamecove.novrr) skips it.

exclude.msi-claw-a8: AMD GPU: the boot hook runs before xe/i915 only, and the A8's panel EDID isn't in the validated list.

changes.detail: A copy of the panel's own EDID with only the refresh range changed to 30-120 Hz.
Which board and connector the EDID is for.
A tiny board check that runs right before the GPU driver loads.
Runs the hook before xe / i915.
The four files above, so it also works when the driver loads early.
The switch the hook looks for (plus firmware_class.path=/etc/firmware, shared with the gyro fix).

fixes.undo: Takes out the kernel argument, the initramfs entries and every file, in reverse order. The panel's own EDID is back after a restart.

probe.what: Reads the panel's own EDID. If it already says 30 Hz or lower (a BIOS that corrected it), nothing is needed. With GameCove's copy in place the factory EDID can't be read, so a BIOS change is checked by a maintainer.

watch.note: A new BIOS may correct the EDID's range (the factory sha256 in panels.txt then stops matching).
Same panel in the Claw 8 AI+.
Panel quirk tables: a kernel quirk for CSW PN8007QB1-2 would replace the EDID override.
Kernel patches naming the panel.

fixes.title: Gyro aiming
fixes.line: Turns on the motion sensor so you can aim by tilting the Claw.
fixes.symptom: The Claw 8 EX's IMU sits behind the Intel sensor hub with MSI firmware Linux doesn't load, so there is no gyro.
fixes.why: MSI's Panther Lake ISH firmware (installed under this model's own ish_ptl_<vendor>_<product>.bin name) and the 2247-byte sensor descriptor of board MS-1T91; Lunar Lake and Meteor Lake Claws use other sensor hubs.
fixes.risk_note: Installs MSI's own sensor-hub firmware (downloaded from MSI, checked by sha256) and changes boot configuration. Only loads on this exact board.

changes.detail: MSI's sensor-hub firmware under this model's own name, downloaded from MSI and checked by size and sha256.
Adds a firmware search path (shared with the VRR fix).
The firmware file, for an early-loading sensor hub.
A HID-BPF program that labels the hub's sensors as accelerometer and gyro.
Keep the sensor powered and correct its drift.
Adds the gyro as a motion source.

fixes.undo: Stops and removes both services, the HID-BPF program, the firmware file, its initramfs entry and the kernel argument (when the VRR fix doesn't need it), and rebuilds the InputPlumber override without the gyro.

probe.what: Looks for a gyro (gyro_3d) that works without GameCove's firmware and HID-BPF program. With the fix in place that can't be told apart, so new linux-firmware and kernel releases are checked by a maintainer.

watch.note: Kernel sensor-hub driver: native support for the Claw's custom sensors would replace the HID-BPF program.
linux-firmware may start shipping MSI's Panther Lake ISH firmware (intel/ish/).
The stock config: an imu source there means InputPlumber expects a native gyro.
A BIOS update can change the sensor hub's firmware needs.

fixes.title: Volume buttons don't wake it
fixes.line: Stops a bump of the volume buttons from waking the Claw in your bag.
fixes.symptom: The volume buttons are keys on the i8042 keyboard, which is a wakeup source, so pressing them wakes the Claw from sleep.
fixes.why: Every MSI Claw (controller 0db0:1901/1902) puts its volume keys on the i8042 keyboard, which is a wakeup source.
fixes.risk_note: One udev rule; the power button still wakes the Claw.

changes.detail: Switches off wake-up for the built-in keyboard port (serio, atkbd) on MSI MS-1T* boards.
Set to disabled at once; the old value is saved.

fixes.undo: Deletes the rule and writes the saved value back.
fixes.bazzite: Not fixed: Handheld Daemon switched it off at start, InputPlumber (Bazzite 44+) doesn't.
fixes.steamos: Not fixed (no Claw support in SteamOS).

probe.what: Looks for the same rule from the system itself (any udev rule that isn't GameCove's and does the same), or the value already being right without GameCove.

watch.note: InputPlumber's udev rules: it may start switching the keyboard wake-up off, as Handheld Daemon did.
Bazzite's handheld udev rules: a Claw wake-up rule would make this os-fixed.
The kernel quirk was refused in 2025-06 in favour of a udev rule; a new attempt would show up here.

fixes.why: Intel Claws (MSI firmware with an Intel Wi-Fi card): the card drops into D3cold during sleep and doesn't come back.
fixes.risk_note: One udev rule. The Wi-Fi card uses a little more power while the Claw sleeps.

fixes.title: Less drain while asleep
fixes.line: Lets the controller chip power down in sleep. Needs controller firmware 319+ (Ally X 313+); checked first.

fixes.why: Every ROG Ally controller MCU behind asus-armoury / asus-wmi mcu_powersave.
fixes.risk_note: With old controller (MCU) firmware the controller can stay dead after waking, so the fix refuses to install until the firmware is new enough (Ally 319, Ally X 313, as the kernel's hid-asus).

fixes.title: Touch in the right place
fixes.line: Makes touch line up with the picture in Gaming Mode (it's turned 90 degrees).
fixes.symptom: gamescope-session-plus marks this sideways panel as external, so gamescope turns the picture but not touch input.
fixes.why: gamescope-session-plus device-quirks starts these OneXPlayer / AOKZOE panels as PANEL_TYPE=external with ORIENTATION=left, so touch isn't turned with the picture. Confirmed on the OneXFly F1 (Bazzite 5581); offered on the other models in such blocks.
fixes.risk_note: One session file that only sets the panel type, checked against the DMI ids.

changes.detail: Sets PANEL_TYPE=internal for this handheld, so gamescope turns touch with the screen.

fixes.undo: Deletes the file. Takes effect next time Gaming Mode starts.
fixes.bazzite: Not fixed (issue 5581; waits for ChimeraOS/gamescope-session PR 128).
fixes.steamos: Not affected the same way (SteamOS uses its own session).

probe.what: Reads gamescope-session's own device-quirks file: once it treats this handheld's panel as internal, nothing is needed.

fixes.title: Keep GameCove off the game's cores
fixes.line: While a game runs, GameCove's own work moves to the efficiency cores at low priority.
fixes.symptom: GameCove's background work could land on a performance core next to the game's render thread.
fixes.risk_note: Only moves GameCove's own process; no system file changes.

changes.detail: While a game runs: CPU affinity to the efficiency cores and nice 10 (taskset, renice). Nothing is written to disk.

fixes.undo: Affinity and priority go back when the game ends, or at once when you switch it off.

fixes.why: A firmware and graphics-driver problem on the 7840U and newer GPD boards; no software workaround is known.
